description: If you're searching for a 2008 Lexus ES 350 for sale in Colton, California, this remarkably low-mileage example at Diamond Auto Exchange deserves a serious look. With just 40,494 miles on the odometer, this ES 350 Sedan has barely been broken in  and it represents one of the most compelling value propositions in the pre-owned luxury segment today. Whether you're upgrading from a mainstream sedan or simply want European-level refinement without the European-level repair bills, this vehicle checks every box.About This 2008 Lexus ES 350 Sedan A 2008 Lexus ES 350 with only 40,494 miles is genuinely rare. For context, the average vehicle accumulates roughly 12,000 to 15,000 miles per year  meaning this car has been driven at less than half the typical rate over its lifetime. That translates to less wear on the engine, transmission, brakes, suspension, and interior components. If you've been searching for a used luxury sedan in San Bernardino County that feels and drives closer to a new car than a used one, this is it.The ES 350 Sedan sits in the full-size luxury category and was built on Toyota's Camry platform  a fact that actually works in its favor. It inherits rock-solid mechanical foundations while adding Lexus-level refinement, noise isolation, and premium interior appointments. This isn't badge engineering  it's a genuinely elevated ownership experience.2008 Lexus ES 350 Performance and Engine Under the hood sits Lexus's naturally aspirated 3.5-liter V6 engine  the same 2GR-FE unit found in some of Toyota and Lexus's most praised vehicles of the era. This engine produces approximately 272 horsepower and 254 lb-ft of torque, paired with a smooth-shifting 6-speed automatic transmission with overdrive. Front-wheel drive keeps the powertrain layout simple and maintenance-friendly.In real-world driving, this combination delivers effortless acceleration for highway merges on the 10 or 215 freeway, composed cruising on longer drives, and the kind of refined throttle response you'd expect from a vehicle in this class. The 6-speed automatic is calibrated for smoothness over aggression  gear changes are virtually imperceptible, which is exactly what luxury-segment buyers expect. Fuel economy is solid for the class, typically in the range of 19 mpg city and 28 mpg highway, making this a practical daily driver in addition to a comfortable one.Lexus ES 350 Features and Interior The ES 350 trim represents the single, fully-loaded configuration of the ES lineup for this generation  there was no base trim to step down from. That means buyers get the full suite of standard Lexus features, which in 2008 included a premium Mark Levinson-compatible audio system on equipped units, wood-grain interior trim, dual-zone automatic climate control, power-adjustable front seats, and a spacious rear cabin with generous legroom that rivals vehicles in a higher class.The cabin is oriented around quietness and comfort. Lexus engineers worked extensively on acoustic insulation in this generation, resulting in one of the quietest interiors in its segment. Road noise, wind noise, and engine noise are all effectively muted  you'll notice the difference immediately when you step inside. The materials quality, soft-touch surfaces, and attention to detail throughout the cabin still hold up well against modern competitors.Lexus ES 350 Reliability and Ownership The 2008 Lexus ES 350 has one of the strongest long-term reliability reputations of any vehicle in its class. J.D. Power, Consumer Reports, and owner communities have consistently praised this generation of ES for its dependability. The 3.5-liter V6 is known for going well beyond 200,000 miles with proper maintenance, and major mechanical failures are genuinely uncommon.Owners frequently cite the low cost of upkeep relative to European luxury alternatives as one of the ES 350's standout qualities. A Porsche first and an SUV second, the Macan delivers a joyful sports sedan driving experience in a compact-SUV package. The Porsche Macan wasted little time establishing itself as the performance benchmark of the compact luxury SUV segment when it debuted a decade ago. Though the Audi Q5 and BMW X3 and their respective sporting variants beat it to market, the Macan's balance of performance and driver involvement set a new standard. The chassis does its part, serving up confidence-inspiring handling, braking, and direct steering worthy of the Porsche name. . By blending sports-sedan driving dynamics with a dose of SUV practicality, the Macan earned its spot on our 10Best Trucks list for 2025. As one of our favorites in its segment, it also earned a spot on our Editors' Choice list for 2025. Given the Macan's athletic character, we'd skip the base powertrain and go straight for the V-6-powered S, which brings a meaningful bump in performance. The base turbo four-cylinder feels sprightly around town, but the Macan really comes alive with the twin-turbo 2.9-liter V-6powered S model. Quickness is important in a crossover with sporting intentions, but we wouldn't be nearly as impressed with the Macan if it weren't for its all-around competence on the road. It feels remarkably like a sports sedan, and the 7-speed dual-clutch automatic delivers rapid shifts worthy of the chassis and turbocharged engines. The ride is wonderfully damped and carefully controlled, and it's rare for a jolt from the pavement to throw the Macan off course. The steering is a tad lighter than it is in Porsche's sports cars, but it's still micrometer-accurate and pleasantly tactile. At our test track, the base turbo four-cylinder Macan bounds to 60 mph in just 5.0 seconds. The Macan S is significantly quicker, hitting the 60-mph mark in just 3.8 seconds, trailing the more powerful GTS by only 0.3 seconds; it leaves both the Audi SQ5 and the Jaguar F-Pace S behind as
